extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys/agents) involved in prosecution and petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural standards and criteria governing USPTO reply deadlines, resetting/restarting reply periods, express/formal abandonment, petitions to revive or reset periods, refund requests, and related special situations during patent prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal holiday and weekend rule for deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Any action or fee due on a Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday is considered timely if taken or paid on the next succeeding day which is not a Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists Federal holidays under 5 U.S.C. 6103; when a holiday falls on a Sunday the following Monday is a holiday; when a holiday falls on a Saturday the preceding Friday is considered a holiday and the USPTO is closed that day. The Saturday/Sunday/Federal holiday is endorsed on the file wrapper with the date of receipt and indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inauguration Day special rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 6103(c), Inauguration Day (January 20, every 4 years) is a legal public holiday for purposes of statutes relating to pay and leave of employees employed in the District of Columbia and surrounding areas; if it falls on a Sunday the next day selected for observance is considered a legal public holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No provision is made for Inauguration Day falling on a Saturday; affects calculation of deadlines when relevant to District of Columbia observance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reset when Office action contains error affecting ability to reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reference citation is incorrect or an Office action contains some other error that affects applicant’s ability to reply and this error is called to the Office’s attention within 1 month of the mail date, the Office will restart the previously set period to run from the date the error is corrected, if requested by applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the error is called to the Office’s attention within the period but more than 1 month after the action, the Office will set a new period substantially equal to the time remaining (must be at least 1 month). Example: error brought 5 weeks after mailing — set a new 2-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remailing of action establishes new reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: When it becomes necessary to remail any action, the action should be correspondingly redated because the remailing date establishes the beginning of the period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing, see IFW Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary action after rejection establishes new statutory date
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplementary action after a rejection that explains the references more explicitly or gives reasons more fully (even if no further references are cited) establishes a new date from which the statutory period runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplementary Office action creates a new running period for replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction after expiration does not restart period without extension fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If an error in citation or other defective Office action is called to the Office’s attention after the expiration of the period for reply, the period will not be restarted and any appropriate extension fee will be required to render a reply timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office letter correcting the error will note that the time period for reply remains as set in the previous Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to reset period due to late receipt — timing and evidentiary criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a petition to restart the previously set period to run from the date of receipt at the correspondence address when: (A) the petition is filed within 2 weeks of the date of receipt; (B) a substantial portion of the set reply period had elapsed on the date of receipt (e.g., at least 1 month of a 2- or 3-month period); and (C) the petition includes evidence showing the date of receipt and a statement setting forth the date of receipt and explanation of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of evidence: copy of Office action stamped with date of receipt, copy of envelope with date stamped. See MPEP § 707.05(g) for correcting record where erroneous citation occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resetting shortened statutory periods (>30 days) — limited availability
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no statutory requirement that a shortened statutory period of longer than 30 days be reset due to mail delay, but when a substantial portion of the period had elapsed, the late-receipt procedures may be available; where an Office action was received with less than 2 months remaining in a shortened 3-month period the period may be restarted; if remaining between 2 and 3 months, reset only in extraordinary situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extraordinary situations include, for example, a complex Office action suggesting submission of comparative data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to reset period due to postmark date later than mail date printed on Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a petition to restart the period to run from the postmark date shown on the Office mailing envelope when: (A) the petition is filed within 2 weeks of receipt; (B) the reply period was for payment of the issue fee, or the reply period set was 1 month or 30 days; and (C) the petition includes evidence of date of receipt, a copy of the envelope showing the postmark date, and a statement that the Office action was received in the postmarked envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.8 and 1.10 apply to the filing requirement that the petition be filed within 2 weeks. The showing may be insufficient if circumstances point to delay after receipt rather than mail delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence may be insufficient if delay appears to be after receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: The showings outlined for petitions to reset may not be sufficient if there are circumstances pointing to a conclusion that the Office action may have been delayed after receipt rather than delayed in the mail or Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should consider alternative explanations and may deny petitions where evidence suggests internal delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment rule under 37 CFR 1.135
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant fails to reply within the time period provided under § 1.134 and § 1.136, the application will become abandoned unless an Office action indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment can result from failure to reply or insufficiency of reply as a 'complete and proper reply' under 1.135(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution to save application from abandonment must be complete and proper
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution to save an application from abandonment pursuant to 37 CFR 1.135(a) must include such complete and proper reply as the condition of the application may require; admission or refusal to admit amendments after final or any amendment not responsive to the last action will not save it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only a timely and fully responsive submission can prevent abandonment; see MPEP § 714 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide but incomplete reply — possible new time under § 1.134
rubrics_metrics.description: When reply by the applicant is a bona fide attempt to advance the application and substantially a complete reply but some matter or compliance was inadvertently omitted, applicant may be given a new time period for reply under § 1.134 to supply the omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.95 rather than the abandonment paragraph when reply appears to be a bona fide attempt with inadvertent omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment requirements (37 CFR 1.138) — who may sign
rubrics_metrics.description: A written declaration of abandonment must be signed by a party authorized under § 1.33(b)(1),(b)(3),(b)(4) to sign a paper in the application; a registered attorney or agent not of record may, in limited representative capacity under § 1.34(a) when filing a continuing application, expressly abandon the prior application as of the filing date granted to the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express abandonment may not be recognized by the Office before date of issue or publication unless actually received in time to act; ensure correct identification of application in the letter of abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment to avoid publication — timing and petition
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid publication under 37 CFR 1.138(c), a declaration of express abandonment and petition (with fee) must be received by appropriate officials in sufficient time to recognize the abandonment and remove the application from the publication process; generally must be received more than four weeks prior to projected publication date to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly advised to file electronically via EFS-Web to increase likelihood of timely recognition; petitions filed within four weeks are unlikely to be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and acknowledgement of letters of express abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: When a letter of express abandonment (not in issue) is received and complies with 37 CFR 1.138, Office personnel should acknowledge receipt using PTO-1432 and check appropriate boxes; if not compliant a fully explanatory letter should be sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional applications should be reviewed prior to filing requests to abandon prior applications because express abandonments are viewed as deliberate acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of all claims is not express abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all claims, even if signed by applicant and assignee, is not an express abandonment and is regarded as nonresponsive and not a bona fide attempt to advance the application to final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will not enter an amendment that cancels all claims without presenting any new or substitute claims; see Ex parte Lassell and Exxon Corp. v. Phillips Petroleum Co.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment after payment of issue fee requires petition under 37 CFR 1.313(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: If express abandonment is submitted in an allowed application after payment of the issue fee, the abandonment must be accompanied by a petition to withdraw from issue under 37 CFR 1.313(c) and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(h); the express abandonment may not be recognized unless received in time to withdraw the application from issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition should be addressed to Office of Petitions; transmission methods include mail, facsimile, hand-delivery, or EFS-Web. If 1.313 precludes effect, remedy is petition under 37 CFR 1.183 showing extraordinary situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of search fee and excess claims fee under 37 CFR 1.138(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant seeking refund of the search fee and excess claims fee by abandoning an application filed on or after Dec 8, 2004 must submit a declaration of express abandonment by way of petition under 1.138(d) before an examination has been made; certificate of mailing/transmission date under § 1.8 is not taken into account for determining timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not filed before examination, Office may retain entire fees. A petition must be filed before an examination is 'made' and a two-month non-extendable period applies for requesting refund after declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'examination has been made' for § 1.138(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Examination has been made' occurs once an action (e.g., restriction/election requirement, requirement under 1.105, first Office action on the merits, notice of allowability/allowance, or action under Ex parte Quayle) is shown in the PALM system as having been counted; if action is counted the same day as the petition, petition was not filed before examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PALM status >031 shows an action counted. Technical preparations for publication generally begin 4 months prior to projected publication date. Form PTO/SB/24B recommended and EFS-Web recommended for filing petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment in interference — inventor signature required
rubrics_metrics.description: A written declaration of abandonment signed only by an attorney or agent of record, when the application is the subject of an interference under 35 U.S.C. 135, is not effective to terminate the interference; to be effective the abandonment must be signed by the inventor with written consent of assignee where there has been an assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment does not terminate interference unless proper inventor/assignee signature exists; such abandonment is not considered until ex parte prosecution is resumed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms for filing express abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/24A may be used for petition for express abandonment under 37 CFR 1.138(c) to avoid publication; Form PTO/SB/24B may be used for filing petition under 1.138(d) to obtain refund of search and excess claims fee; Form PTO/SB/24 may be used for letter of express abandonment or in favor of a continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recommended forms; EFS-Web filing recommended where timing is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive for unavoidable failure to reply (37 CFR 1.137(a)) — contents and showing
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive on grounds that failure to reply was unavoidable must be accompanied by: (1) the required reply (filed); (2) a showing to Director that entire delay from due date until filing of a grantable petition was unavoidable; (3) any required terminal disclaimer; and (4) the petition fee as set forth in 1.17(l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The showing can be statements of fact establishing that the delay was unavoidable and inadvertent. No consideration given until fee received. Terminal disclaimer and fee apply in certain situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive for unintentional failure to reply (37 CFR 1.137(b)) — contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive on grounds that the failure to reply was unintentional must be accompanied by: (1) the required reply (filed); (2) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional; (3) any required terminal disclaimer; and (4) the petition fee as set forth in 1.17(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may require additional information where there is question whether delay was unintentional. Use cover letter 'Petition to Revive.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer required for revival in certain applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer and fee under 37 CFR 1.137(d) is required if the application is: (1) a design application, (2) a utility application filed before June 8, 1995, or (3) a plant application filed before June 8, 1995. The terminal disclaimer must dedicate to the public a terminal part of the term equivalent to the period of abandonment and must also apply to any patent granted on any application containing a specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c) to the application for which revival is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimer must be submitted with the petition and fee; relevant to certain pre-June 8, 1995 filings and design/plant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and limit rules for extensions of reply periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which a petition under 37 CFR 1.136(a) and the appropriate extension fee have been filed is the date for determining the period of extension and the corresponding amount of the fee. In no case may an applicant reply outside the SIX (6) MONTH statutory period or obtain an extension for more than FIVE (5) MONTHS beyond the date for reply set forth in an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fully responsive reply must be timely filed to avoid abandonment. Examiner notes: do not mail abandonment until extension period under 1.136(a) has expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency of reply may cause abandonment — examiner form guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be abandoned where applicant's reply is within the period for reply but is not fully responsive to the Office action. Use form paragraph 7.91 for 'Reply Is Not Fully Responsive' and include examiner reasoning; if reply is bona fide attempt with inadvertent omission use form paragraph 7.95 instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should set forth why reply is considered failure to take 'complete and proper action' and pull application for abandonment after expiration of maximum permitted period for reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special situations that often lead to abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Various situations can cause abandonment: (A) copying claims from a patent when not suggested by the Office does not constitute a reply; (B) withdrawal of or failure to prosecute an appeal to the Board can result in abandonment; (C) dismissal of an appeal or civil action can cause abandonment unless amendment was filed prior to dismissal; (D) claims suggested for interference near end of reply period; (E) filing a CPA under 1.53(d) (considered express abandonment of prior application as of filing date of continuing app); (F)-(H) improper filing of an RCE (without fee or necessary submission) may be treated as withdrawal of appeal or may not toll time periods and can result in abandonment or failure to toll time for issue fee payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP sections referenced (e.g., §1215, §201.06(d), §706.07(h)) for detailed handling; improper RCE will not toll running of prior time periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of proceedings (copendency) definition under 35 U.S.C. 120
rubrics_metrics.description: A second application is considered copending with an earlier application if it is filed before (A) the patenting, (B) the abandonment of, or (C) termination of proceedings on the earlier application. 'Before' has consistently been interpreted to mean 'not later than.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition affects whether later applications can claim benefit/copedency to earlier filings.
